public_comment.topic: Proposed extending the sewer line up Pond Street to serve a planned duplex development (an ANR subdivision) near the old driving range on Wham, asking whether the commission would extend the sewer district and eventually give its blessing before a town meeting warrant article.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of 2/24 and the joint select board meeting minutes of 3/3

budget_items.what_was_said: The commission reviewed the proposed FY27 rate, keeping the minimum charge increase at 5% while raising the regular usage charge more (about 16%), shifting more of the burden to higher water users. Staff said the rate is driven by what Leominster and Fitchburg charge Lunenburg for sewer treatment.
Demand fee notices will be mailed the week of March 16th; residents who have not paid their sewer bill were asked to pay before Friday, in person or online.

The commission recapped that it had already voted the FY27 budget in at a prior meeting so it could go out with the town warrants; a budget presentation was scheduled for Thursday night before FinCom. The budget avoids using retained earnings this year, with capital gains funding slightly reduced.

Members noted betterment revenue is slowing down as fewer new betterments come in, which is part of what is pushing the rate increases; the goal was described as trying to keep rates level rather than see dramatic swings.

budget_items.topic: Capital projects - Pump 2 and manhole covers
budget_items.what_was_said: Upcoming capital work includes work at Pump 2 and resetting manhole covers; the wrong size covers had been ordered but the correct size is in the warehouse and ready to install, targeted around April 15th.

An existing manhole repair contract is targeting manholes previously inspected and suspected of having inflow and infiltration (I&I); a member pushed for a more proactive approach to find and fix leaks rather than just tracking rising charges from Fitchburg/Leominster.

If a storm water utility is established, residents would be billed separately, similar to a sewer bill, with revenue used to fund street sweeping, storm drain cleaning and other work needed for federal storm water permit compliance.

budget_items.topic: Cost of special permit / engineering for duplex proposal
budget_items.what_was_said: The developer said he did not want to spend roughly two years and about $100,000 pursuing a special permit, preferring an as-of-right ANR approach; he said he is open to spending tens of thousands of dollars on engineered plans and to commission review of them.

decisions.decision: Recommended the developer file a citizen's petition warrant article by March 16th to make the May 2nd town meeting deadline.
Developer asked to return to the March 31st commission meeting so the commission could consider giving its "blessing" to the sewer extension plan ahead of town meeting.
Demand fee notices to go out the week of March 16th.
Sewer bylaw wording amendment (two words changed for consistency with the new ADU bylaw), already reviewed by town counsel, to proceed to town meeting for a vote.
Set upcoming meeting dates: March 31, 2026 (Zoom); April 14, 2026 (in-person/hybrid); April 28, 2026 (Zoom); May 12, 2026 (in-person/hybrid).

minutes.headline: Sewer Commission weighed extending sewer service for a proposed duplex development via town meeting warrant article
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission spent most of the meeting on a developer's request to extend sewer service up Pond Street to serve a planned duplex subdivision, discussing a possible town meeting warrant article and whether the commission would support it once engineered plans are ready. The commission also reviewed FY27 user rate and budget updates, ongoing infiltration/inflow and manhole repair work, a minor sewer bylaw wording change tied to the new ADU bylaw, and the pending storm water utility warrant article, approving prior minutes and adjourning by roll call.

what_happened.line: The Commission recommended the developer file a citizen's petition warrant article by March 16 to extend sewer service up Pond Street for a proposed duplex subdivision.
The developer was asked to return March 31 so the Commission could consider giving its "blessing" to the extension plan before town meeting.
A sewer bylaw wording change tied to the new ADU bylaw, already reviewed by town counsel, is headed to town meeting for a vote.
The FY27 sewer rate proposal shifts more of the increase onto higher water users, and this year's budget avoids drawing on retained earnings.
A separate storm water utility fee, which would bill residents apart from the sewer bill, is also headed to a town meeting warrant article.

why_it_matters: Extending sewer service to a new subdivision is a decision residents will see as a warrant article at the May 2 town meeting.
The FY27 rate structure and bylaw changes affect what appears on sewer bills and how future accessory dwelling units connect to the system.
A new storm water utility fee would be a separate charge on top of the existing sewer bill if adopted at town meeting.
